from_statement: DRAFT explicit obstruction kept mathematically by independent referee w413 on 2026-10-10; integration's served-model/different-model gate remains unestablished. This is a counterexample to a general inference, not to the percolation conjecture. For 0<=t<1/2, set Y=sqrt(4-8t), W=3-3Y/2, g_t(1)=3-Y and g_t(2)=3-Y/2. The real Loewner equations hold: g_t(1)'=2/(Y/2) and g_t(2)'=2/Y. Their distances from W have ratio 1/2, so the single Cardy observable C((g_t(1)-W)/(g_t(2)-W)) is the constant martingale 1/2. W is nonconstant deterministic finite variation with zero quadratic variation, so one such observable cannot identify a Brownian driver without further premises. For a third mark starting at 3, the initial ratio derivative is -2/27, and its Cardy observable is not a martingale.
